summary: Parkevtate Vosianc asks whether BigBear.ai (BBAI) is finally a buying opportunity after its third consecutive quarter of revenue growth, noting the stock is down over 50% year-to-date in 2026 and that he has warned all year it was too expensive. Revenue rose 31% in the quarter, management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $150–165 million for the first time — about 23% growth at the midpoint — and backlog reached $330 million, up 22% from the prior quarter. Gross margins improved by 878 basis points and the cash-flow-to-sales ratio improved after years of deterioration, though the company still loses money, holds almost $400 million in cash and short-term investments, and trailing-twelve-month revenue of $142 million remains below its mid-2023 peak of $162 million. He sizes the opportunity at roughly $140 billion, combining $112 billion of expected 2027 US defence AI and autonomy spending with a global aviation security market growing from over $17 billion in 2026 to $27 billion by 2031. Valuation is still rich at a forward price-to-sales ratio of 6.8 versus rivals, though cheaper than in 2025. His discounted cash flow fair value rose to about $2.50 against a current price of about $2.45 — the auto-captions garble these as $25 and $245 — so the stock is converging on fair value but not there yet. Call: BBAI AVOID at about $2.45, fair value about $2.50, with another solid quarter potentially earning an upgrade to BUY.
